tone_statements.citation: Hofmann, Erica. 1990. A Preliminary Phonology of Bana. MA thesis, Department of Linguistics, University of Victoria. xii+275 pp. (SIL Cameroon scan; SIL archive no. 9718; downloaded from Internet Archive copy of silcam.org)
tone_statements.quote: That Bana has two contrasting tones, high and low, is easily demonstrated. All tone patterns are possible for all parts of speech, but monomorphemic uninflected verbs prefer simple tone patterns. Phonetic rising and falling tones, which are rare, are best analyzed under an autosegmental approach as two tones docking on a single syllable. [...] (6.4) Bana, then, has two contrasting tones, high and low, which may occur in any tone pattern. The phonetic contour tones are in fact only combinations of simple tones.
tone_statements.locator: Chapter VI 'Tone', opening paragraph, thesis p. 93 + section 6.4 'A Two Tone System', thesis p. 101; abstract p. iii also states 'Bana is a tone language, having two contrasting tones'
tone_statements.n_tones: 2 (H, L); phonetic rising/falling = HL/LH sequences on one syllable

sources.citation: Gravina, Richard. 2014. The Phonology of Proto-Central Chadic. LOT Dissertation Series 375. Utrecht: LOT.
sources.note: Nothing on Bana stress. Sec. 6.5.1 'Bana' (pp. 166-167) summarises Hofmann 1990 (three vowels /ə e a/, syllable-level palatalization prosody, labialized velars); the work explicitly excludes tone and stress from its reconstruction.

sources.citation: Green, Christopher & Steven Moran. 2019. Bana sound inventory (GM 1248) [from Hofmann 1990]. In: Moran, Steven & Daniel McCloy (eds.), PHOIBLE 2.0. Jena: Max Planck Institute for the Science of Human History.http://phoible.org/inventories/view/1248
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: Segment table of the GM 1248 inventory lists four tone entries: high (MODIFIER LETTER HIGH TONE BAR), low (LOW TONE BAR), high-low falling and low-high rising - i.e. it codes Bana as tonal with H, L and two contours, extracted second-hand from Hofmann 1990 (who herself treats the contours as H+L / L+H sequences, not tonemes).
